title: Ravensgate warehouse robot command stream

act2.summary: compliance restricts contraband pickups to the inspection zone - a new legality rule, unaffected by how commands are applied or inverted

solutions.title: One shared function decides whether a command is even legal
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that command legality was the pressure most likely to grow a new business exception, and pulled it into one function shared by runCommand and replayBatch's forward pass. The inspection-zone rule arrives on exactly that axis: one new clause, in the one place a command's legality is decided, at 3 lines in a single hunk.

solutions.title: One shared function decides what a command does to the robot's state
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that how a command changes state - forward or inverted, across four call sites - was the pressure worth relieving first, and pulled it into one function every apply site calls, including the batch rollback and undoLast. The inspection-zone rule doesn't touch what a command does, only whether it's allowed to happen at all - refund-by-reason branching was never touched, so it still duplicates the new clause across runCommand and replayBatch's own validation, at exactly the no-pattern baseline's cost.

reviewFocus: Does the reader's own restructuring name, honestly, which pressure it chose to relieve - legality, or effect/inverse - and admit the other is still duplicated?
Would a reader who restructured command-effects instead of command-rules still recognize, from the measured numbers alone, why the inspection-zone rule landed cheaply or expensively?
Does the WALKTHROUGH.md for the losing route say plainly that its bet didn't pay off for this act 2, without pretending its own restructuring was worthless in general?
Do both routes agree, byte for byte, with src/ on every act-1 outcome before the inspection-zone rule exists?
Does the reader's own rollback logic actually replay each undone command through the same apply/invert rules as the forward path, rather than special-casing it?
